judged_text: remove_member deletes rows via group.users.delete(user_id) directly on the association collection, bypassing the GroupUser model's destroy callbacks and the Group#remove path used elsewhere. Any logic that runs when a user leaves a group (e.g. automatic group title removal / group-user observers) is silently skipped, so admins removing members via the new UI leave stale titles and derived state behind; the next maintainer changing GroupUser lifecycle will not realize this controller sidesteps it.

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#remove_member the diff removes a user via `group.users.delete(user_id)` (association-level delete) instead of using the group’s higher-level removal API (`group.remove(user)` used elsewhere in the prior controller code). This is a real, diff-grounded design/maintainability concern because it sidesteps any encapsulated removal logic and (by Rails semantics) can bypass join-model destroy callbacks, so lifecycle side effects may not run for admin removals.
